audit_notes: Model: classic shear-lag of a platelet of length L in a mortar under the thermal-mismatch strain of the coating: s'' = beta^2 (s - E_p*eps), with stress-free platelet ends s(0)=s(1)=0 (x normalised by L). beta^2 = 2 G_m L^2/(E_p t_p t_m) = 5.33 for the audited values, beta = 2.31; the maximum platelet stress is E_p*eps*(1 - 1/cosh(beta/2)) = 0.43*E_p*eps = 26 MPa, below the strength of alumina/mica platelets (~300 MPa+). Baseline: conventional continuous mineral (silicate) film of the same phases, represented by a rigidly bonded/long platelet: shear_lag_factor 5000 (beta ~ 71), giving s_max ~ E_p*eps = 60 MPa, i.e. the level at which brittle silicate paints craze. Mortar shear strain = eps*L/(2*t_m) = 4e-4*8e-6/4e-8 = 8 percent - high for a hybrid mortar; creep/ageing of the mortar under UV is the real limit. Important: this computes a mechanical stress in the coating, not the heat gain. Its link to the objective is indirect (fewer cracks -> slower reflectance and weathering loss); the thermal benefit estimate of ~6 percent is not simulated. Dimensionless: beta = 2.31, platelet aspect ratio 20. Simulation coefficient: beta^2 = 5.33. Solver: analytical (linear ODE, closed form). Audit passed.
